title: Evidence First: Vietnam Needs Transparent Dog-Trade Reform
excerpt: Claims about stolen pets, poison bait, and rabies risks require named records and dates. Public safety still demands quarantine, enforcement, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
No verified arrest, seizure, conviction, poison-bait incident, or health alert appears in the supplied material. That absence blocks honest reporting of a specific victim or scene. It does not erase the duty to protect families, pets, and communities from illicit transport, theft, unsafe handling, and weak quarantine enforcement.

Myths need records, not repetition

“Tradition” cannot excuse criminal pet theft, illegal transport, or regulatory breaches. “Farm-raised dogs” cannot serve as proof without traceable records, veterinary oversight, origin documents, quarantine compliance, and lawful slaughter controls. Claims that every animal enters trade through theft also require case records; they must not be presented as established fact without named investigations or judgments.

Official evidence must identify dates, locations, agencies, charges, court outcomes, seizure totals, and health findings. Without those details, campaigners should reject both trade propaganda and unsupported counterclaims. Vietnamese families and local reform leaders deserve facts strong enough to support enforcement and lasting policy.

Biosecurity cannot depend on slogans

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. See WHO guidance.

Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains are separate dimensions of biosecurity failure. One cannot prove the other. Both demand transparent investigation, veterinary controls, lawful transport, and accountability for offenders.

Demand proof. Demand protection.

Sign SDE's petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers. Sign the national petition.
